title: Version 4 has no delivery wave, and Architecture v5 puts Epics 2 and 3 in one wave while the plan gives each epic its own monthly release
source: Recovery Workbench Release Plan v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Releases sheet; resulting new Waves sheet
description: Version 4 is a release calendar only: eight monthly releases, one per epic, with no wave. Architecture v5 slide 38 sets four service waves plus Wave 0, and states Wave 2 as Epics 2-3, Wave 3 as Epics 4-5 and Wave 4 as Epics 6-7, so a wave spans two or three monthly releases while the plan releases once a month. Template and Rules R5.6 maps business epics to waves the same way (EP01 to 1, EP02 and EP03 to 2, EP04 and EP05 to 3, EP06 to EP08 to 4). No source read states which release starts a wave or how a wave boundary is written on a monthly release, so version 5 states the boundary as the first release of the wave's first epic and records the position here.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 38: 'Wave 1 - Epic 1', 'Wave 2 - Epics 2-3', 'Wave 3 - Epics 4-5', 'Wave 4 - Epics 6-7' and note 'Waves follow the first epic of each module'; Template and Rules R5.6 gives the same map by business epic; Release Plan v4 Releases sheet holds one row per epic E1 to E8 with one release date each and no wave column; Release Plan v4 Calendar sheet holds the same eight epics with no wave.
proposed: Confirm that a wave starts at the first release of its first epic (Wave 2 at E2, Wave 3 at E4, Wave 4 at E6) and keep the eight monthly releases with their dates; if the programme instead releases once per wave, E2 and E3 merge and the calendar is rewritten.

title: The plan has no Wave 0 row and no platform release, so nothing states when the platform enablers are complete
source: Recovery Workbench Release Plan v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Releases sheet (starts at E1); Gates sheet; resulting new Waves sheet
description: Architecture v5 makes Wave 0 the enabler: service template, Helm chart, contract libraries, workflow kit, 19 schemas and logins, Kafka topics and ACLs and Temporal 1.30+, all before Wave 1. Version 4 has no platform release and no Wave 0 row: its first release is E1 on 30 November 2026 and its gates G1 to G6 are all per release. No source read gives a date by which Wave 0 must be complete, so version 5 states it as the E1 go decision, 27 November 2026, taken from the E1 row of the plan, and records the position here rather than inventing a platform release.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 38: 'Wave 0 - now. Platform once. Service template + Helm, Contract libraries, Workflow kit (L3), 19 schemas + logins, Kafka topics + ACLs, Temporal 1.30+'; Template and Rules R5.1 lists seven platform epics RWB-PLT-TPL to RWB-PLT-OBS; Release Plan v4 Releases sheet first data row is E1 with build start 2 November 2026, go decision 27 November 2026 and release 30 November 2026; the plan's Gates sheet has no platform or wave gate.
proposed: Add a Wave 0 row to the plan with its own entry and exit criteria, owned by the platform epics of R5.1, and confirm that Wave 0 completes before the E1 go decision.

title: No source states who approves a published contract or that a release gate covers contract publication
source: Recovery Workbench Release Plan v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Gates sheet, new gate G7 Contract published
description: Architecture v5 requires every service to publish its OpenAPI, AsyncAPI and activity contracts with a fake before code, and Template and Rules R5.4 makes a contract dependency (class C) non-blocking, which only works if a published contract exists. Version 4 has six gates per release and none of them covers contract publication, and no source read names the role that approves a contract version or the artefact where it is published. Version 5 adds gate G7 Contract published, decided by the code owner of the owning service with the solution architect, and records the missing approval route here.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11: 'Every service publishes its contracts (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, activity jar) before code; contract tests run in every build'; Template and Rules R5.4 class C: 'Build against the published contract and its fake. Blocks the build? No'; Template and Rules R5.7 rules 1 and 2 make a CON story Day 1; Release Plan v4 Gates sheet holds G1 Design signed to G6 Benefit check only; no source read names a contract approver or a contract artefact store.
proposed: Name the contract approver role and the artefact store, then confirm gate G7 with that role as its decider and cite it from every CON story of the wave.

title: The Features and Stories counts, and the 'Delivered in' text, are monolith-era and are not restated per service
source: Recovery Workbench Release Plan v4; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (stats); Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Releases sheet columns Features and Stories; Modules by release sheet column Delivered in
description: The Releases sheet counts 118, 77, 31, 50, 26, 37, 18 and 19 features and 60, 31, 31, 50, 26, 37, 18 and 19 stories by epic, and the Modules by release sheet says when each module is delivered in epic terms ('E1 core, E2 screens'). Both are written for the monolith and its story split. The realignment splits the same legacy work into 1,034 story slices over 358 legacy stories, one service per module, so the plan's counts no longer describe the realigned backlog and the 'Delivered in' text mixes a module with several service releases. No source read gives a per-service or per-wave count, so version 5 keeps every number and every 'Delivered in' text unchanged and records that they are monolith-era counts.
evidence: Release Plan v4 Releases sheet: Features 118, 77, 31, 50, 26, 37, 18, 19 and Stories 60, 31, 31, 50, 26, 37, 18, 19; split_plan.json stats: slices 1,034, legacy 358, day1 939, lanes 510; Modules by release sheet rows P3 'E1 core, E2 screens' and S2 'E2 foundations; E3'; Template and Rules R5.1 and R5.2 replace the module with the service and the story ID pattern.
proposed: Restate the counts per release from the realigned story set once the Service Story Catalog v1 is assembled, and keep the version 4 numbers as the legacy baseline beside them.

title: The plan names no owner per release, and no source states which team owns a wave's release readiness
source: Recovery Workbench Release Plan v4; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Releases sheet (no owner column); Gates sheet column Who decides; resulting new Waves and Services by release sheets
description: Version 4 names the roles that receive users and the roles that decide each gate, but no owner per release, per epic or per module. The realignment turns each module into a service with an owner in the Ownership Map v1, and Template and Rules R5.3 gives each work type a suggested team, with no person named anywhere. No source read states who owns a release's readiness across the services of a wave, so version 5 records the service owner codes and the team types as the owner position and leaves the accountable role for a release open.
evidence: Release Plan v4 Releases sheet columns: Epic, Theme, Status, Design signed by, Build starts, SIT week from, UAT week from, Go decision, Release, Modules and content, What the business gets, Features, Stories, Roles that receive real users, Calendar and dependency notes; Ownership Map v1 Services sheet gives a code and a service for each of the 19 modules and no person; Template and Rules R5.3 fixes the owner phrase '(suggested; any team may pick up this story)'; AGENTS.md rule 4 forbids the name of a person.
proposed: Name the release owner role for each wave in DL48 and the release record, with the service owner codes of the wave as the delivery owners and no person named.

title: Version 5 carries no approval and the source records no status
description: The source workbook has no status, approval or sign-off statement anywhere in its five sheets: the Releases sheet has a Status column per epic (Confirmed for E1 and E2, Proposed for E3 to E8) but no status for the plan itself, and no approval record. The realignment run takes no approval stop. Version 5 therefore states Status Draft with the open approval as a gap and an assumption, and keeps the per-epic status words of the source unchanged.
evidence: Release Plan v4 Releases sheet Status column: E1 Confirmed, E2 Confirmed, E3 to E8 Proposed; no other sheet carries a status, approval or sign-off row; workbook properties modified 15 November 2026 with no approval field.
proposed: Record the approval of version 5 by the programme and the delivery lead with a date, and keep a Status row in every later version.

title: The source carries no change log and no tool line
section: Read me sheet (new); change log table
description: Version 4 has no change log, no version history and no tool line, so there is no record of what changed between version 3 and version 4. Version 5 adds the change log, records version 4 as the source row with that gap, and gives its own row the D-RCV-60 change and the tool line required by Template and Rules R8.1.
evidence: The five sheets of version 4 are Releases, Modules by release, Gates, Calendar and Release rules; none holds a change log, a revision history or a tool line; the workbook title is 'Recovery Workbench Release Plan v4' and the properties record created 27 October 2026 and modified 15 November 2026.
proposed: Keep the change log in every later version and reconstruct the version 3 to version 4 change from the document properties and the release record.

title: Version 4 gives S4 rwb-litigation notice approval in E2 while Architecture v5 creates S4 in Wave 3
source: Recovery Workbench Release Plan v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Releases sheet row E2 (Modules and content); Modules by release sheet row S4; resulting new Waves and Services by release sheets
description: The E2 row of version 4 lists 'S4 notice approval' and the Modules by release sheet gives S4 'E2 notices; E5', so the E2 release needs part of rwb-litigation. Architecture v5 slide 38 creates S4 in Wave 3 with Epics 4-5, and slide 41 puts rwb-litigation in wave 3. Template and Rules R5.6 resolves a story whose business-epic wave is earlier than its service's wave in favour of the business epic and asks for one conflict gap per service and business epic, which is this row. Version 5 keeps the E2 content of the source unchanged, marks S4 as a Wave 3 service with E2 work, and records the position here.
evidence: Release Plan v4 Releases sheet E2 Modules and content: 'S4 notice approval'; Modules by release sheet S4: 'E2 notices; E5'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 38 'Wave 3 - Epics 4-5: S1 Valuation, S3 Guarantee, S4 Litigation, S6 Debt sale' and slide 41 gives S4 rwb-litigation wave 3; Template and Rules R5.6: 'A story whose W-MAP wave is earlier than its service's Arch v5 wave keeps the W-MAP wave. One conflict gap is raised per service and business epic.'
proposed: Either bring the S4 service creation forward to Wave 2 so that E2 notice approval has a service, or move the E2 notice approval to E5 and keep S4 in Wave 3; record the choice in the Decision Log against DL44 and DL48.
